title: After more than a decade of computing power transformation, Lenovo's quarterly revenue tops 200 billion yuan for the first time, with net profit soaring 166%
excerpt: Lenovo Group today announced results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026/27: quarterly revenue topped RMB 200 billion for the first time, up nearly 50% y
content_html:
Lenovo Group today announced results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026/27: quarterly revenue topped RMB 200 billion for the first time, up nearly 50% year over year; adjusted net profit exceeded RMB 9 billion, surging 166% year over year, while net margin rose 2 percentage points to 4.5%. Both set new records. Chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing immediately sent an internal letter setting the tone: "When it comes to AI, Lenovo is in it to win it." The most eye-catching figure: AI-related revenue rose nearly 80% year over year and already accounts for 36% of the group's total.

All three business groups are breaking records

By segment, ISG (Infrastructure Solutions Group) revenue climbed to 2.8 times the year-earlier level, operating profit crossed RMB 7 billion for the first time with a 9.6% margin, and AI server order backlog reached RMB 530 billion; IDG (Intelligent Devices Group), despite a decline in unit sales, still grew revenue 15%, further widening its lead over the No. 2 player in global PC share; SSG (Solutions and Services Group) posted a record operating margin of 26%.

Yang pointed to a structural shift: ISG and SSG now account for more than 60% of the combined operating profit of the three groups. Lenovo has completed its transformation from a "PC leader" to a "global leader in full-stack computing power," and the market has begun to reprice it.

On the outlook, his judgment was quite confident: AI is moving from training to inference, and cloud providers and enterprise customers are investing heavily in compute buildout; in the era of AI agents, data and compute will increasingly be generated on devices and at the edge, making Lenovo's complete "device-edge-cloud" layout perfectly timed.

The internal letter ended by setting out a goal—striving to reach $100 billion in revenue ahead of schedule this year. The tailwind that a decade of planning has been waiting for is now blowing hard.
